entities.summary:
Annibale di Ceccano (Annibaldo Caetani di Ceccano) was an Italian Cardinal of the Catholic Church, serving as a high-ranking cleric in the medieval hierarchy. He played a crucial role in the papal court during the 14th century, navigating the complexities of power, politics, and religious influence.





The Livrée Ceccano, a grand palace built in the 1330s, served as Ceccano's residence and a center of power in Avignon, France. This palace, now a public library, stands as a testament to Ceccano's wealth and influence. The Livrée Ceccano was one of the largest and most impressive palaces in Avignon, featuring intricate architecture, ornate decorations, and a grand courtyard.





Ceccano's contributions to the Catholic Church were significant, particularly in the areas of diplomacy and theological debate. He was a key figure in the papal court, working closely with other high-ranking clergy to shape church policy and resolve conflicts. Ceccano's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the development of the Catholic Church and its relations with European monarchies.





In his later years, Ceccano became embroiled in a series of disputes with other cardinals, ultimately leading to his resignation from the papal court. Despite this, his impact on the Church's history remains substantial, with many regarding him as a pivotal figure in the medieval papacy.
